Glycolysis

The enzyme phosphofructokinase is rate-limiting for glycolysis and its activity follows v = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]) where Km is the Michaelis constant and x2 marks a squared term.[1] Afterwards the pathway continues towards pyruvate.

Energy and mass are related by E = mc2 while the variance is σ2 = E[(X − μ)2] for any random variable.

Hexokinase phosphorylates glucose to glucose six phosphate inside the cell.
